rationale: The hypothesis claims that marked structural central nervous system malformations are absent in FILIP1-related neuromuscular disorder with congenital dysmorphic facies (NMDCF), facilitating distinction from congenital muscular dystrophies with brain involvement. However, Roos et al. (2023) explicitly document that affected individuals with biallelic FILIP1 variants present with 'brain malformations' alongside neuromuscular features and developmental delay. Because the provided literature documents structural brain malformations but lacks granular neuroradiological breakdowns in the available text to verify whether lissencephaly or cobblestone cortex specifically occur or are definitively absent, the hypothesis is conflicted and cannot be fully substantiated.

evidence.text: Patients with biallelic FILIP1 variants present with core neurological features that explicitly include structural brain malformations, in addition to neurodevelopmental delay, muscle weakness, and dysmorphisms.

source.title: Bi-allelic variants of FILIP1 cause congenital myopathy, dysmorphism and neurological defects
source.quote: Patients exhibit a broad spectrum of neurological symptoms including brain malformations, neurodevelopmental delay, muscle weakness and pathology and dysmorphic features.

evidence.text: FILIP1 disruption leads to a syndromic neuromuscular disorder with dysmorphism and neurological involvement, reported also in the context of paternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 6.

evidence.text: Homozygous loss-of-function variants in FILIP1 are associated with syndromic arthrogryposis and neuromuscular phenotypes in consanguineous/recessive disease cohorts.

source.title: Systematic analysis of homozygous autosomal copy number losses in exomes improves diagnostic yield and uncovers ultra-rare recessive disorders

conflicts: Roos et al. (2023) describe brain malformations as a prominent phenotypic feature of biallelic FILIP1 disease, contradicting the assertion that structural CNS malformations are absent.
The available excerpts do not specify whether severe cobblestone lissencephaly or dystroglycanopathy-like CNS malformations can be definitively ruled out without neuroimaging review.

new_directions.question_text: What specific neuroradiological patterns (e.g., ventriculomegaly, corpus callosum hypoplasia, posterior fossa anomalies, or cortical dysplasia) characterize FILIP1-associated brain malformations on brain MRI?
new_directions.rationale: Resolving the exact neuroimaging findings in all reported FILIP1 cohorts is necessary to determine whether cortical migration defects occur and how reliably brain MRI discriminates NMDCF from alpha-dystroglycanopathies.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact numerator and denominator frequencies of individual dysmorphic, neuromuscular, and CNS imaging findings across all published FILIP1 patients?
new_directions.rationale: Establishing comprehensive HPO-standardized phenotype frequency tables across cohorts will enable objective clinical differentiation from overlapping congenital myopathies and syndromic arthrogryposis disorders.
